message.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial-intelligence-based visual inspection systems increasingly use auxiliary confidence and evidence signals to rank predictions for limited human review. In safety-relevant engineering inspection, however, these review layers are commonly validated end-to-end under image degradation, even though the same degradation simultaneously changes both the evidence signal and the classifier error population. This study introduces a channel-separated validation framework for trustworthy AI-based inspection, using railway surface-defect assessment as the engineering application. A 2×2 audit independently perturbs the task and evidence pathways and evaluates the incremental utility of the evidence layer against a matched softmax-derived baseline under group-disjoint nested cross-validation. On 932 rail-head images, severe sensor noise caused a complete conclusion reversal: with the classifier error population held fixed, the clean-calibrated engineering evidence fell 0.326 AUROC below the baseline, whereas conventional end-to-end evaluation placed the same evidence 0.397 above it. The reversal occurred in all 25 repeated folds and was independently reproduced with a self-supervised DINOv2 Vision Transformer (-0.305 versus +0.532). The effect was corruption-dependent and was not reproduced under motion blur. Rare-class removal and multiclass decision-geometry analyses showed that sensor-noise-induced reshaping of the error population largely generated the apparent end-to-end benefit, while a prospectively locked DINOv2 analysis supported the proposed geometric boundary condition. A corrected public RSDD experiment provided an external boundary case in which no comparable reversal occurred. These results show that end-to-end robustness testing alone can mischaracterize the reliability of human-review evidence layers and motivate channel-separated auditing before deployment of AI inspection systems.</jats:p>
title: Channel-separated validation of the human-review layer in automated rail inspection under acquisition shift
